messages:
maria: Heads-up: CS ticket CS-3419 — multiple customers saw short 503 bursts on hosted inference starting ~09:20 UTC.

oncall-olivia: PD fired at 09:19. Dashboards show spike in 503s across us-east-1 / eu-west-1 / ap-southeast-1, peak ~09:22. Investigating.

deploy-bot: deployment/hosted-infer v2.14.0 rolled at 08:58 UTC (canary -> global). Rollout currently paused.

kai: Pulled pod logs from one restart:

```
infer-runner[1423]: starting prefetch for model redwood-v1-7B
infer-runner[1423]: prefetch waiting for device sync
kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 1423 (python) total-vm:xxx
kubelet: Container \"infer-runner\" failed liveness probe
infer-runner[1423]: received SIGTERM: shutting down
```

sam: Seeing both OOM kernel lines and SIGTERM. Two things could be happening: prefetch stalls health check -> kubelet kills -> SIGTERM, or high memory causing OOM -> kill.

maria: No automatic coredumps. kubectl describe shows liveness probe timeouts right before termination.

cs-jordan: Customers reported long tail latency then timeouts, then 503s. All using hosted-prod keys.

oncall-olivia: Quick repro in staging:

```
# hammer prefetch with big ctx + concurrency
for i in 1..60; do curl -s -X POST $STAGE/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-7B","input":"'$(python -c \"print('x'*15000)\")'"}' &
done
```
Health endpoint latency jumps >10s, liveness fails.

kai: v2.14 changed prefetch sync to block on device to avoid stale KV races. Under concurrent prefetch this blocks the main thread handling /healthz.

sam: So root cause: blocking prefetch starves health path leading to kubelet SIGTERM. In a subset of cases the prefetch also causes host memory pressure and OOM.

maria: Impact level P2. CS escalated. What's the emergency mitigation?

oncall-olivia: Actions taken at 09:40 UTC:
- Paused global rollout and stopped canary progression.
- Emergency patch: liveness probe timeout raised from 10s -> 45s.
- Deployed a lightweight health responder on a separate thread to avoid being blocked by prefetch.

deploy-bot: emergency/hosted-infer-liveness-patch applied to clusters at 09:43 UTC.

cs-jordan: Customers reporting service recovered after ~09:46. Marking CS-3419 as mitigated; offering regen credits for affected windows.

kai: Long term fixes proposed:
- Move prefetch to dedicated async worker pool (non-blocking).
- Add memory limits and prefetch throttling to avoid host OOMs.
- Improve graceful shutdown to dump state / request tracing on SIGTERM.

sam: I'll open the following PRs:
- PR #4520: prefetch -> async executor
- PR #4521: prefetch mem limiter + fallback (reduced batch)
- PR #4522: isolate health endpoint thread

maria: Logging/runbook notes:
- Collect kubectl logs + previous for all restarted pods
- Extract kernel logs (/var/log/kern.log) for OOM kills
- Map proxy traces to pod IDs and affected API keys
- Enable core dump collection if SIGSEGV/OOM reappears

oncall-olivia: AIs:
- kai: prototype async prefetch (ETA 48h)
- sam: land health-isolation + prefetch timeout (ETA 24h)
- infra: add coredump collection runbook (INFRA-289)
- cs: outbound customer notice + credits

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged. Status -> mitigated / monitoring.

maria: Do not resume the global rollout until the fix is validated in canary under high concurrency for 24h.

sam: Labels added: incident/runtime, cause:prefetch-block, mitigation:timeout-thread

kai: I'll attach a small repro harness in PR that simulates concurrent large-context prefetches.

maria: Thanks — will file postmortem and link here when draft ready (incident-2024-09-prefetch-sigterm).
